raw.excerpt: About Nebius:Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy.
raw.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

The Forward Deployed Engineer, Cloud Platform is a senior, high-autonomy individual contributor role that owns the infrastructure foundation making the physical AI platform fast, reliable, scalable, secure, and cost-effective. This role sits with strategic customers and ISV partners, embedded directly inside their engineering teams, and ships production infrastructure that lets customers run real physical AI workloads, not just demos. Your job is to make the platform feel like a product, not a collection of cloud scripts.

You will work alongside the Field CTO and the Head of Physical AI, and partner closely with the Physical AI Systems and Platform & Product FDEs. Inside each account, you own end-to-end technical execution: discovery, scoping, infrastructure design, build, and production rollout. Across accounts, you turn repeated infrastructure pain into reusable platform capabilities and partner with Product and Engineering to fold them into the core platform. Your field work is the primary input to the Nebius Physical AI roadmap.

You are welcome to work remotely from the United States (SF Bay Area, CA or Austin, TX preferred).

Your responsibilities will include:

  • End-to-End Ownership Inside Strategic Accounts: Own discovery, technical scoping, infrastructure design, build, and production rollout for each design partner and ISV engagement, translating ambiguous infrastructure problems into deployable production systems.
  • Cloud Infrastructure & Compute Orchestration: Build and operate the cloud infrastructure that powers customer physical AI workflows. Own compute orchestration for simulation, training, evaluation, inference, and batch workloads, not just what runs, but how it runs at scale.
  • Platform Services: Build platform services for job execution, scheduling, retries, observability, logging, secrets, access control, and cost tracking. Integrate Nebius cloud services into the product experience so infrastructure complexity is abstracted away from customers.
  • Customer Onboarding Infrastructure: Build onboarding infrastructure for pilots, including sandbox environments, dataset storage, workflow execution, and deployment, and make sure early customer workloads run for real: secure, isolated, observable, and reliable.
  • Reliability, Security & Cost: Optimize cloud cost, utilization, performance, and reliability across workloads, and debug infrastructure issues across application, network, storage, compute, and orchestration layers, wherever the failure actually lives.
  • Cross-FDE Partnership: Partner with the Physical AI Systems FDE to support GPU-heavy simulation, training, and evaluation pipelines, and with the Platform & Product FDE to expose infrastructure capabilities through clean APIs, SDKs, and product workflows.
  • Long-Term Architecture: Help define the long-term infrastructure architecture for multi-tenant SaaS, enterprise deployments, and high-throughput physical AI workloads.
  • Pattern Codification & Productization: Turn repeated customer infrastructure pain into reusable platform capabilities. Partner with the Field CTO, Product, and Engineering teams to fold these into the core platform. Treat every engagement as a forcing function for the next ten.
  • Rapid Engineering Velocity: Use modern AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) as primary leverage. Compress build timelines from weeks to days. Treat engineering velocity as a primary success metric.
  • Field Enablement & Feedback Loops: Co-author reference architectures, solution templates, and technical blogs for the broader Nebius field, and maintain structured channels to ensure customer learnings flow back to the Field CTO, Product, and Engineering teams.


We expect you to have:

  • 6+ Years of Hands-On Engineering: Strong backend, cloud infrastructure, platform engineering, or SRE experience, with at least two years in a customer-facing or deployment-oriented technical role (Forward Deployed Engineer, founding engineer, technical co-founder, tech lead embedded with strategic customers, or equivalent).
  • Distributed Systems & Compute Platforms: Experience building distributed systems, job orchestration, compute platforms, internal developer platforms, or ML infrastructure.
  • Strong Systems Programming: Strong Python, Go, or similar systems and backend programming skills.
  • AI-Native Development Workflow: Fluency in modern AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) as primary leverage to rapidly design, implement, test, debug, and refactor production-quality software.
  • Cloud-Native Toolchain: Experience with Kubernetes, containers, CI/CD, observability, cloud networking, storage, IAM/RBAC, and infrastructure as code.
  • GPU & HPC Workloads: Familiarity with GPU workloads, batch jobs, training pipelines, inference workloads, or HPC-style compute environments.
  • Cross-Layer Debugging: Proven ability to debug infrastructure issues across application, network, storage, compute, and orchestration layers.
  • Security & Reliability Instincts: Strong instincts for isolation, RBAC, uptime, and traceability on workloads that touch customers.
  • High Agency: You navigate ambiguity without waiting for permission, with a bias toward simple, composable infrastructure that serves real customer workflows over scheduling another meeting.
  • Communication: Strong written and verbal communication. You can hold your own in a technical conversation with a customer CTO and debrief a design partner engagement to the Head of Physical AI.

It would be an added bonus if you have:

  • Prior experience as a Forward Deployed Engineer or an equivalent customer-embedded engineering function at a frontier company.
  • Experience with Nebius, AWS, GCP, Azure, Lambda Labs, or other AI cloud infrastructure.
  • Experience with Slurm, Soperator, Kubernetes GPU scheduling, Ray, Argo, Airflow, Metaflow, or similar orchestration tools.
  • Experience with ML training infrastructure, model serving, simulation workloads, or large-scale data pipelines.
  • Experience supporting enterprise customers, design partners, or production pilots.
  • Familiarity with NVIDIA GPU infrastructure, CUDA workloads, Isaac Sim, Omniverse, or simulation-at-scale.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

Equal Opportunity Statement:

Nebius is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace and to providing equal employment opportunities in all aspects of employment. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Swanson, and V8.

Here, you will make a difference every day. You will be supported to build a rewarding career with opportunities to grow, innovate and inspire. Make history with us.

An Agentic AI Engineer designs, builds, and deploys autonomous AI systems that can reason, plan, use tools, and execute multi-step workflows with minimal human intervention . Unlike traditional AI/ML engineers who focus on model training and prediction, agentic AI engineers orchestrate goal-driven workflows that integrate models, tools, memory, and business logic to achieve objectives dynamically


Core Responsibilities

  • Design & Develop Agentic Systems: Build intelligent agents capable of autonomous planning, reasoning, and task execution, often using LLMs (e.g., GPT-class, LLaMA), multi-modal models, and autonomous workflows
  • Orchestration & Frameworks: Implement agent orchestration using frameworks like LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel, or custom solutions
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): Design and optimize RAG pipelines for enhanced reasoning with external knowledge, including document ingestion, chunking, embeddings, vector stores, and retrieval ranking
  • Tool & Memory Integration: Develop agents that call APIs, databases, and other tools, maintain memory, and adapt based on outcomes
  • Evaluation & Monitoring: Create evaluation frameworks for accuracy, grounding, latency, and cost; build observability for agent behavior and failure modes
  • Model Adaptation: Fine-tune or adapt foundation models (e.g., via LoRA, adapters) for domain-specific use cases
  • Production Deployment: Deploy GenAI/agentic systems in cloud-native environments with CI/CD, versioning, and runtime safeguards
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work with data scientists, ML engineers, product teams, and governance/compliance stakeholders

Required Skills & Experience

  • 2+ years in AI/ML system design, deployment, or autonomous agent development
  • Programming: Proficiency in Python (and sometimes Java, C#) for AI/ML solution development
  • Agent & Workflow Expertise: Experience with agent orchestration frameworks and multi-agent communication protocols
  • RAG & LLM Integration: Hands-on with RAG architectures, evaluation methodologies, and LLM integration
  • Cloud & DevOps: Experience with cloud platforms (e.g., Azure, AWS) and CI/CD pipelines
  • Governance & Compliance: Understanding of responsible AI, security, and compliance in regulated domains (e.g., retail)

raw.excerpt: BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals.
raw.description:
BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals. When considering candidates, we look for scientific and business professionals who are highly motivated, collaborative, and most importantly, share our passionate interest in fighting cancer.

GeneralDescription:

The Director, Technology Business Management is responsible for establishing and leading BeOne’s financial management, consumption strategy, cost transparency, and value optimization capability across foundational technology services. This includes public cloud, data centers, network, compute, storage, observability, backup and recovery, managed services, infrastructure platforms, software tooling, and related technology services.

This role partners with Infrastructure, Cloud Engineering, Network, Enterprise Architecture, Cybersecurity, Finance, Procurement, Data, AI, Application, and Business Technology teams to improve technology cost visibility, optimize consumption, strengthen financial accountability, and align infrastructure investment with business value. The Director will lead the development of Technology Business Management and FinOps practices, including forecasting, budgeting, showback/chargeback, cost allocation, unit economics, vendor commitment management, cost optimization, consumption governance, and executive reporting.

EssentialFunctionsoftheJob:

Technology Business Management & Financial Governance

  • Establish and lead a Technology Business Management and FinOps operating model across foundational technology services.
  • Develop financial governance practices for cloud, data centers, network, compute, storage, observability, backup, managed services, and infrastructure platforms.
  • Partner with Finance and Technology leaders to create budgets, forecasts, variance reporting, and financial performance reviews.
  • Define and manage showback, chargeback, cost allocation, and cost transparency models for major technology services and business consumers.
  • Establish standards for cost center mapping, service taxonomy, tagging, metadata, account/subscription structure, and allocation methodology.
  • Build executive-level reporting for technology spend, consumption trends, savings opportunities, forecast risks, and investment tradeoffs.
  • Drive accountability for technology consumption across platform, application, data, AI, business, and regional teams.

Infrastructure Consumption Strategy & Cost Optimization

  • Develop consumption strategies that balance cost, performance, reliability, security, compliance, and speed of delivery.
  • Identify and lead optimization opportunities across cloud, data centers, network circuits, compute, storage, databases, observability, backup, AI/HPC, and managed services.
  • Partner with engineering teams to implement automated rightsizing, scheduling, cleanup, lifecycle management, capacity planning, and demand management.
  • Manage cloud and infrastructure commercial levers, including savings plans, reserved instances, committed use discounts, enterprise agreements, software licensing, vendor commitments, and service-provider optimization.
  • Support vendor negotiations by providing consumption analytics, forecast modeling, benchmark analysis, scenario planning, and commitment recommendations.
  • Establish workload-level and service-level unit economics to help technology and business leaders understand cost-to-serve.
  • Develop policies and guardrails to reduce waste, prevent cost leakage, and improve financial discipline across infrastructure platforms.

Cloud FinOps

  • Lead the FinOps capability across public cloud platforms, including AWS, Azure, GCP, and related cloud-native services.
  • Establish cloud cost visibility, tagging compliance, budget controls, anomaly detection, cost optimization backlog management, and savings realization tracking.
  • Partner with Cloud Platform Engineering to embed cost controls into landing zones, infrastructure-as-code modules, deployment pipelines, and platform guardrails.
  • Support cost-aware architecture patterns for cloud-native applications, data platforms, AI/ML workloads, databases, network egress, storage tiers, and observability services.
  • Provide guidance on cloud account/subscription structure, cost allocation, shared services, commitment coverage, and workload economics.
  • Develop dashboards and reporting that make cloud cost, utilization, waste, and optimization opportunities visible to engineering and leadership teams.

Datacenter, Network, & Foundational Infrastructure Economics

  • Establish cost management practices for data center hosting, colocation, compute, storage, backup, disaster recovery, monitoring, and infrastructure tooling.
  • Partner with Network Engineering to manage telecom, WAN, SD-WAN, internet, private connectivity, cloud connectivity, and network service costs.
  • Support data center and hosting strategy decisions through financial modeling, total cost of ownership analysis, lifecycle planning, and consumption forecasting.
  • Partner with infrastructure operations to evaluate managed service provider costs, service levels, demand patterns, and operational efficiency.
  • Develop standard service-cost models for foundational infrastructure capabilities.
  • Identify opportunities to rationalize platforms, reduce duplicate tooling, retire unused services, and improve vendor value realization.

Planning, Analytics, & Executive Reporting

  • Build financial models, consumption forecasts, cost baselines, and scenario plans to support annual operating planning and strategic investment decisions.
  • Provide monthly and quarterly executive reporting on technology consumption, optimization progress, savings realization, forecast accuracy, and investment risks.
  • Track realized savings, avoided costs, cost optimization backlog, unit-cost trends, vendor commitment utilization, and consumption risks.
  • Develop KPIs and scorecards for financial performance, forecast accuracy, allocation quality, tagging compliance, utilization, optimization, and value realization.
  • Translate complex technical consumption patterns into clear financial and operational insights for senior leadership.
  • Support business cases for cloud migration, data center modernization, platform automation, network transformation, resilience investment, and AI/data platform expansion.

Governance, Process, & Continuous Improvement

  • Define processes, roles, decision rights, governance forums, and escalation paths for Technology Business Management and FinOps.
  • Establish recurring cost and consumption review cadences with infrastructure, cloud, network, application, data, AI, finance, procurement, and business stakeholders.
  • Develop standards, playbooks, and procedures for cost reviews, budget alerts, anomaly detection, optimization intake, savings validation, commitment management, and cost allocation.
  • Promote a culture of cost awareness, financial accountability, and continuous improvement across engineering and technology teams.
  • Evaluate and implement TBM, FinOps, cost management, reporting, and automation tools as needed.
  • Monitor industry practices, cloud provider capabilities, infrastructure economics trends, and emerging technology financial management practices to continuously mature BeOne’s capabilities.

SupervisoryResponsibilities:

  • Team Leadership: Lead and develop a Technology Business Management and FinOps team responsible for cost management, consumption analytics, optimization execution, financial governance, and executive reporting.
  • Recruitment and Onboarding: Support recruiting, hiring, onboarding, and role clarity for team members.
  • Task Assignment: Assign work based on business priorities, team capacity, financial impact, technical complexity, and stakeholder needs.
  • Support and Resource Provision: Ensure team members have the tools, data access, training, documentation, and stakeholder support required to perform effectively.
  • Communication and Collaboration: Promote strong collaboration across Infrastructure, Cloud Engineering, Network, Finance, Procurement, Cybersecurity, Enterprise Architecture, Application, Data, AI, and Business Technology teams.
  • Performance Evaluation: Conduct regular performance discussions, provide constructive feedback, and measure team outcomes against agreed objectives.
  • Mentoring and Development: Coach team members in TBM, FinOps, infrastructure economics, analytics, stakeholder management, executive communication, and financial governance.
  • Issue Resolution: Resolve prioritization, data quality, process, stakeholder alignment, and accountability issues promptly and constructively.
  • Career Development Support: Support professional development, certifications, and career growth for team members.

Computer Skills: Proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, and financial reporting tools. Advanced Excel, data analysis, dashboarding, and executive reporting skills required. Experience with tools such as Power BI, Tableau, Apptio, Cloudability, CloudHealth, Flexera, ServiceNow, AWS Cost Explorer, AWS Cost and Usage Reports, Azure Cost Management, Google Cloud Billing, Datadog Cloud Cost Management, native cloud billing tools, or equivalent platforms preferred.

EducationRequired:

Bachelor’s degree or higher in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, Finance, Business Administration, Economics, Data Analytics, or a related discipline. Advanced degree preferred.

OtherQualifications:

  • Fluent in written and verbal English.
  • Minimum 10 years of relevant experience in technology, infrastructure, cloud operations, finance, procurement, analytics, technology business management, or related functions.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience with cloud financial management, infrastructure cost management, technology consumption governance, or technology business management.
  • FinOps Foundation certification, TBM certification, cloud provider certifications, ITIL, or equivalent professional certifications preferred.
  • Experience leading TBM, FinOps, cloud cost management, infrastructure financial governance, IT finance, technology operations analytics, or related functions.
  • Strong understanding of foundational technology services, including public cloud, data centers, network, compute, storage, backup, observability, managed services, and infrastructure platforms.
  • Strong understanding of public cloud pricing models, including compute, storage, networking, database, observability, AI/ML, managed services, and enterprise commitment structures.
  • Experience with AWS required; experience with Azure, GCP, multi-cloud, data center, and network cost management preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to partner with Finance, Procurement, Engineering, Cybersecurity, Enterprise Architecture, Application, Data, AI, and senior technology leadership.
  • Strong analytical, financial modeling, communication, and executive presentation skills.
  • Ability to translate complex technical consumption patterns into business, financial, and operational insights.
  • Experience building dashboards, KPIs, governance processes, executive reporting, and business cases.
  • Understanding of infrastructure architecture, cloud operating models, DevOps, infrastructure-as-code, platform engineering, network architecture, service management, and vendor management.
  • Experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, life sciences, healthcare, or other regulated industries preferred.
  • Familiarity with the FinOps Framework, Technology Business Management practices, IT service costing, cost allocation, and financial governance preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence without direct authority across global, cross-functional teams.
  • Strong results orientation, financial discipline, continuous improvement mindset, and ability to operate in a fast-paced global environment.

Travel: Be adaptable to business trips as required per business need; require valid driver’s

license in applicable countries

Salary Range Poland: 364,200.00 PLN - 455,200.00 PLN

Global Competencies

When we exhibit our values of Patients First, Driving Excellence, Bold Ingenuity, and Collaborative Spirit, through our twelve global competencies below, we help get more affordable medicines to more patients around the world.

  • Fosters Teamwork
  • Provides and Solicits Honest and Actionable Feedback
  • Self-Awareness
  • Acts Inclusively
  • Demonstrates Initiative
  • Entrepreneurial Mindset
  • Continuous Learning
  • Embraces Change
  • Results-Oriented
  • Analytical Thinking/Data Analysis
  • Financial Excellence
  • Communicates with Clarity

We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. BeOne does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, national origin, veteran status or any other basis covered by appropriate law. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business need.

raw.description:
Associate Director, AP Graphics

College Board–Advanced Placement

Location:This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type: This is a full-time term position that will last for 2 years from the start date.

About the Team

The College Board’s Advanced Placement and Instruction division (300+ staff) develops and administers coursework taken by more than 3 million students worldwide each school year, and the related subject-matter exams utilized by more than 4,000 colleges and universities for course placement and awarding of college credit. These include credit and placement examination programs like CLEP and ACCUplacer; Advanced Placement (AP) and Pre-AP courses in 40+ disciplines; and associated teacher professional learning programs.   

The AP Graphics team produces exam and instructional graphics across the full AP course portfolio, and owns the standards, tools, and processes that underpin graphic production for all new and existing AP courses and exams. This team plays a central role in ensuring visual accuracy, accessibility, and production efficiency across every format— digital, hybrid, and paper—from initial course development through final exam delivery.

About the Opportunity

The Associate Director, AP Graphics plays a key role in the AP Assessment Production Graphics workstream, providing flexible, cross-course production support as the team scales. In this role, you will create technical vector graphics, maps, and illustrations across a range of AP courses, adapting quickly to unfamiliar content and shifting priorities as coverage needs require. You will maintain brand and accessibility consistency across your work, and communicate directly with content experts and production colleagues to resolve requests and design issues efficiently. As course assignments shift, you will ramp into new subject matter and production standards on tight timelines, working within a fast-paced, deadline-driven production environment—directly supporting AP's mission to give every student the opportunity to study and learn at the college level.

In this role, you will:

Execute Cross-Course Graphics Production (70%)

  • Handle day-to-day graphic requests across multiple assigned AP courses based on shifting production priorities set by the Senior Director

  • Produce graphics per existing AP Graphics standards established by Senior Director and Course Leads, adapting quickly across formats and course domains

  • Move fluidly between courses as volume, deadlines, or coverage needs require

Support Shared Standards and Documentation (15%)

  • Contribute to and assist in maintaining asset libraries, templates, and documentation across multiple courses, under the direction of the Senior Director in collaboration with Course Leads

Facilitate Problem-Solving and Continuous Improvement (15%)

  • Engage in troubleshooting for technical issues and workflow questions within assigned scope

  • Contribute to team-wide process improvements as capacity allows

About You

  • 3+ years of professional technical art, graphic design, and/or illustration experience

  • Portfolio demonstrating excellent vector graphic and illustration skills

  • Expert-level knowledge of Adobe Illustrator and Adobe Photoshop (Proficiency with Adobe InDesign and other Creative Cloud apps is a plus.)

  • Familiarity with graphics industry conventions for both digital display and print (e.g., resolution, file formats, color modes, typography)

  • Understanding of basic mathematical concepts like scale, angles, ratios, and percentages

  • Competent photo editing skills

  • Strong attention to detail

  • Working knowledge of Smartsheet and/or Sharepointpreferred

  • Familiarity with any AP course subject matter (e.g., STEM, World Languages, Geography) is a strong plus

  • Bachelor's degree in Design, Illustration, or another related field

  • The ability to travel2-4 times a year to College Board offices or on behalf of College Board business

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work

  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.

  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal

  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.

  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.

  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success

  • Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled.This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.

  • While thehiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise such as live coding, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck: we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.

A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $56,000 - $90,000.

  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.

  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.

  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out ourcareers page for more.

Job Title: Coordinator Assistant (HHAeXchange proficiency)

Location: Remote

Employment Type: Full-Time

Work Schedule

Initial Schedule (First 4–6 Weeks)

  • Monday – Thursday: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM EST
  • Friday: 9:00 AM – 12:30 PM EST
  • 45-minute unpaid break

Schedule After 4–6 Weeks

  • Monday – Thursday: 6:00 AM – 5:00 PM EST
  • Friday: 6:00 AM – 5:00 PM EST
  • 45-minute unpaid break

Position Summary

Our client is seeking a highly organized and proactive Coordinator Assistant to support the daily operations of a growing home healthcare organization. This role is ideal for someone with strong experience in home healthcare coordination who can effectively manage physician orders, visit compliance, nursing documentation, and same-day staffing while ensuring continuity of patient care.

The ideal candidate must have a solid understanding of HHA Exchange and be comfortable navigating the platform to support daily operations. This position requires excellent communication, strong follow-up skills, and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Follow up with physicians' offices to obtain signed medical orders.
  • Track and maintain outstanding physician documentation.
  • Review Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) records and resolve missing or incomplete visits.
  • Follow up with nurses and caregivers regarding missing skilled nursing visit notes.
  • Coordinate same-day staffing for open caregiver shifts.
  • Contact available caregivers to fill last-minute scheduling gaps.
  • Maintain accurate documentation of communications and follow-up activities.
  • Communicate professionally with physicians, caregivers, patients, and internal teams.
  • Support daily administrative and operational activities.
  • Ensure compliance with healthcare documentation standards and company policies.

Required Qualifications

  • Minimum 2 years of experience in healthcare coordination, scheduling, home care, or healthcare administration in a US home care practice
  • Strong working knowledge of HHA Exchange is required.
  • Experience following up on physician orders or medical documentation.
  • Experience with Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) and visit maintenance.
  • Excellent verbal and written English communication skills.
  • Strong organizational, multitasking, and time-management abilities.
  • High attention to detail with excellent follow-up skills.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous experience working in a home healthcare or home care agency.
  • Experience coordinating caregivers, HHAs, CNAs, or nursing staff.
  • Knowledge of healthcare compliance and documentation requirements.

Ideal Candidate

  • Highly organized and dependable.
  • Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking skills.
  • Proactive with excellent follow-up abilities.
  • Comfortable communicating with physicians, caregivers, and internal teams.
  • Able to prioritize urgent tasks while maintaining accuracy.
  • Team-oriented with a strong sense of accountability.

Technical Requirements

  • Reliable computer or laptop.
  • Stable high-speed internet connection.
  • Professional headset with microphone.
  • Quiet, distraction-free home office.
